    {"name": "visit_type", "analytical_usefulness": 0.85, "source_groundedness": 0.9, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Categorises encounter type (acute/chronic/preventive), a genuine axis plausibly correlated with visit length. Values match source text well across samples."},
    {"name": "active_problem_count", "analytical_usefulness": 0.8, "source_groundedness": 0.55, "hallucination_observed": true, "rationale": "Problem burden is a reasonable predictor of duration. However groundedness is shaky: the URI note lists essentially one problem (count 1 ok), but the annual physical mapped to 2 despite only fatigue as a symptom, and the acne visit (single condition) shows 2. The count often appears inflated/loosely derived."},
    {"name": "clinical_severity", "analytical_usefulness": 0.85, "source_groundedness": 0.85, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Acuity is a strong candidate signal for visit length. Sample categorisations (low/moderate) are well warranted by the text."},
    {"name": "critical_stabilizing_action", "analytical_usefulness": 0.75, "source_groundedness": 0.6, "hallucination_observed": true, "rationale": "Emergent stabilisation would lengthen visits, so useful. But the acne row labelled 'acute_treatment_in_visit' is a stretch—starting a topical/oral med is routine prescribing, not an in-visit stabilising action; overreads the source."},
    {"name": "imaging_or_diagnostic_ordered", "analytical_usefulness": 0.85, "source_groundedness": 0.7, "hallucination_observed": true, "rationale": "Ordering imaging plausibly extends visits. Echo and MRI rows are correct, but the annual physical labelled 'point_of_care_only' has no POC imaging mentioned—only labs; an invented diagnostic."},
    {"name": "laboratory_test_ordered", "analytical_usefulness": 0.7, "source_groundedness": 0.75, "hallucination_observed": true, "rationale": "A single boolean but a meaningful workup signal for duration. Physical/MI rows (labs ordered) correct; however the knee-injury row marked True has no labs in the text, only MRI—unsupported."},
    {"name": "specialist_consult_urgency", "analytical_usefulness": 0.7, "source_groundedness": 0.75, "hallucination_observed": true, "rationale": "Consult/referral urgency is a plausible length driver. Knee row inferring 'routine_outpatient_referral' is a soft inference from MRI-to-rule-out-tear, not explicitly stated. Largely redundant with specialist_consult_or_referral."},
    {"name": "medication_change_type", "analytical_usefulness": 0.8, "source_groundedness": 0.9, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Med changes require counseling time, relevant to duration. Acne row 'new_medication_started' correct; MI/physical 'not_present' correct."},
    {"name": "counseling_topic_type", "analytical_usefulness": 0.75, "source_groundedness": 0.8, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Counseling content relates to visit length. Categorisations are reasonable readings, though some are inferred (physical→lifestyle) where the note is terse."},
    {"name": "shared_decision_making_documented", "analytical_usefulness": 0.45, "source_groundedness": 0.75, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Mostly false (186/250) and near-constant; weak signal. Sample values conservatively False where text is silent, which is acceptable."},
    {"name": "specialist_consult_or_referral", "analytical_usefulness": 0.45, "source_groundedness": 0.75, "hallucination_observed": true, "rationale": "Strongly redundant with specialist_consult_urgency (same category vocabulary, near-identical distribution), adding little new leverage. Knee referral is an inference not explicit in text."}
  ],
  "analytical_usefulness": 0.75,
  "source_groundedness": 0.75,
  "rationale": "Most added columns give genuine, distinct axes (visit_type, severity, workup ordered, med change, counseling) directly relevant to what drives visit length, so table-level usefulness is solid. Two consult columns are largely redundant with each other and shared_decision_making is near-constant, dragging usefulness down slightly. Groundedness is generally sound—categorical readings track the notes and silent rows default reasonably—but several rows show overreach: invented labs/imaging on the physical and knee rows, an inflated active_problem_count, and a debatable 'acute_treatment' label for routine prescribing. These recurring confident specifics beyond the text keep groundedness at moderate-high rather than high."
}
